title: CAA's Bryan Lourd Urges Congress to Pass the No Fakes Act
excerpt:
The talent agency executive wants federal safeguards against unauthorized AI replicas.
The proposal addresses digital copies of people's voices and likenesses.
body_md:
Creative Artists Agency executive Bryan Lourd has urged US lawmakers to advance the No Fakes Act, proposed legislation intended to address unauthorized digital replicas of people's voices and likenesses. He argues that the issue extends well beyond film stars and recording artists to anyone whose identity can be reproduced using generative AI.

Lourd pointed to examples of people discovering synthetic versions of themselves in advertising without permission. He said the entertainment industry is not opposed to new technology and that some performers are already negotiating consensual agreements for digital versions of their identities.

The central principle, in his view, is that people should retain control over whether their face or voice is used and should be compensated when appropriate. He has called for a consistent federal framework rather than relying solely on a patchwork of state rules.

The measure passed the Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously in June, according to the report, but it still requires further legislative action before becoming law. Supporters cited include SAG-AFTRA, the Motion Picture Association and several technology companies. Its final passage has not been confirmed.
